source: Curated chokepoint dependency and exposure registry
methodology: Country and asset entries combine public bypass capacity, country chokepoint dependence, and analyst-curated routing assumptions. Modeled at-risk volumes are scenario estimates, not measured flows.

exportSystems: Iran Kharg and Bandar Abbas exports
entries.note: Largest global oil chokepoint. Saudi Petroline and UAE ADCOP provide partial bypass, but a closure still strands the majority of Gulf seaborne crude and condensate flows.

exportSystems: Red Sea crude and product flows
entries.note: Bab el-Mandeb is a route chokepoint rather than a production chokepoint. Its macro impact is shipping reroute cost, Red Sea disruption risk, and Suez-linked tightness.
Ruwais is partially insulated by the Habshan-Fujairah bypass. Exposure remains non-zero because upstream Gulf balances tighten even when ADCOP remains available.

entries.exportRoute: Iran south system / Kharg-Bandar Abbas corridor
entries.note: Abadan is effectively Hormuz-locked. No physical bypass exists, and downstream resilience depends on how long Iranian inland storage can absorb upstream disruption.
ADCOP bypass materially reduces Hormuz dependence, but UAE export economics and benchmark pricing remain tightly linked to Gulf balances.
Iran remains fully Hormuz-locked. Export concentration at Kharg and Bandar Abbas makes the country a pure chokepoint dependency case.
